title: Lung diffusion test (DLCO)
what: You breathe in a safe gas mix and hold your breath for 10 seconds. The device shows how well your lungs pass gas into your blood.
why: For shortness of breath with no clear cause, for diseases of the lung tissue, to track treatment, or before some treatments.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; the report is usually ready the same day
tell_doctor: If you smoke and when you last smoked
Anemia or recent blood tests. They affect the result

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Do not smoke on the test day, at least from the morning. Smoking changes the result a lot.

prepare.title: Oxygen
prepare.text: If you use oxygen, say so in advance. They will tell you what to do.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light breakfast. No hard exercise before the test.

bring: A recent blood test, if you have one
steps: You sit, and a clip is put on your nose
You hold the tube with your lips and breathe calmly
On command, you breathe all the way out
You take a quick, deep breath of the gas mix
You hold your breath for about 10 seconds
You breathe out calmly. This is repeated 2 or 3 times with breaks
feel: Holding your breath can be hard. Say so if you cannot manage
The gas mix has no smell and is safe
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
The report is usually ready the same day

faq.q: Is the gas in the test dangerous?
faq.a: No. There is very little of it, and you breathe it out quickly.

faq.q: Why can't I smoke before the test?
faq.a: Smoking changes your blood, and the test will look worse than it really is.

reminders.text: Lung diffusion test tomorrow. Do not smoke from the morning. Bring a recent blood test, if you have one.
